children: Global markets diverged this week, with European stocks posting strong gains on robust corporate earnings, while Asian markets were mixed.
Technology stocks faced selling pressure during the week as inflation concerns and expectations of further Fed tightening weighed on valuations. Among major technology stocks, NVIDIA
retreated, adding to the Nasdaq Composite's weekly decline.
Out of the nine S&P 500 companies in the supplied earnings data with available estimates, all nine beat EPS expectations, while seven surpassed revenue estimates.
For the week, the S&P 500 rose 1.24% to 7,549.48, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.76% to 52,272.23. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.97% to 25,122.17.
The STOXX Europe 600 surged 3.53% for the week, while Germany's DAX

Annual headline producer inflation accelerated to 6.5% from 6.3% in the previous month. The readings reinforced expectations for a December Fed rate increase.

Meanwhile, European equities benefited from strong earnings, with STOXX 600 companies on track for 25% quarterly profit growth, the strongest in four years. Energy companies were a major contributor, while the region's lower technology exposure helped cushion volatility in global AI stocks.
Eurozone GDP expanded 0.4% Q/Q in the third quarter, while UK GDP grew 0.7%.
